citation: Kaslow et al. (2016), CubeSat Model-Based System Engineering (MBSE) reference model - Development and distribution - Interim status
title: CubeSat Model-Based System Engineering (MBSE) reference model - Development and distribution - Interim status
venue_type: conference, 32nd Space Symposium Technical Track, Colorado Springs, Colorado
modeling_scope: System-level CubeSat MBSE reference model. The paper describes a logical SysML framework for CubeSat missions covering stakeholders, needs/objectives/constraints, measures, requirements, use cases, lifecycle stages, phases of operations, CubeSat domain/enterprise, generic space and ground logical architectures, and subsystem decomposition including a power subsystem. It also summarizes earlier RAX work that modeled behaviors, solar-energy collection/storage, subsystem power consumption, communications, simulations, and trade studies.
mbse_language_method_tool: SysML using No Magic graphical modeling tools/MagicDraw; OOSEM as the stated systems engineering method; distribution/interface mechanisms include MagicDraw, ZIP, XMI, OpenMBEE, and Teamcenter. The paper also emphasizes interfaces with other engineering models and simulations.
robot_platform: CubeSat/nanosatellite platform. The paper defines CubeSats as miniature spacecraft based on a 10-cm unit cube, about one kilogram per cube, typically 1U to 3U with some up to 6U; it also discusses the three-unit RAX CubeSat as prior application context.
task_domain: Generic CubeSat mission and systems engineering reference model for future CubeSat developers, educational use, and evaluation on actual CubeSat projects; prior mission context includes RAX ionospheric science and FireSat as a hypothetical example.
interface: The paper states that MBSE integrates requirements and interfaces in a single system model and helps integrate discipline-specific engineering models and simulations. It also identifies distribution/model-exchange interfaces such as MagicDraw, ZIP file, XMI file, OpenMBEE, and Teamcenter, and addresses CubeSat interfaces with ground systems, launch/deploy services, GPS, and relay satellites.
feedback: Model updates are described as automatically propagated into system views; previous phases executed behaviors and constraint equations for operational trade studies. The distribution concept includes user feedback mechanisms from model users back to the SSWG team. No closed-loop EPS or autonomy feedback controller is described.
evaluation: Status/progress paper rather than quantitative validation. It demonstrates the approach through summarized prior phases: SysML application to RAX, behavior simulation, interfaces with commercial simulation tools, executable constraints, and two trade studies on onboard energy versus solar panel/battery parameters and data downlink versus orbit/ground-station network. The current reference model is illustrated with scope, stakeholder, requirement, domain, architecture, and distribution views.
rq_relevance: RQ1: yes, because the paper's main contribution is a generic CubeSat SysML reference model with stakeholder, requirement, lifecycle, operation, domain, enterprise, and logical architecture elements, and it includes a power subsystem and prior power-behavior modeling. RQ2: partial, because it claims MBSE/model integration benefits such as integrating discipline-specific models, automatic propagation of changes, model-generated documentation, reusability, reduced SE burden, and uniformity/consistency, but it does not provide measured reliability outcomes. RQ3: partial, because verification/validation and testing are included at a general system/process level and future model-correctness verification is planned, but EPS-specific verification procedures are not modeled in detail.
claimed_outcomes: Integrability: the system model is claimed to integrate discipline-specific engineering models and simulations and to keep requirements and interfaces in a single model.
Change consistency: the paper claims that changes are automatically propagated and reflected in every view of the system.
Documentation/reproducibility support: the paper states that documentation should be generated from the model rather than the model from documents.

Reuse and consistency: the reference model is claimed to provide logical architecture elements reusable for mission-specific CubeSats and to promote uniformity and consistency across future CubeSat models.
Systems-engineering efficiency: MBSE is claimed to hold promise for reducing the burden of systems engineering tasks for small CubeSat teams.
Reliability outcomes are not reported as measured or explicitly attributed to the model.
verification_validation_linkage: General V&V linkage is present. The paper defines MBSE as supporting requirements, design, analysis, verification, and validation across the lifecycle; the stakeholder model includes a Tester responsible for V&V; the Cal Poly Design Specification model includes testing requirements; the reference model supports pre-launch integration and test; and next steps include verifying model correctness. EPS-specific verification procedures are not reported.
key_findings: The INCOSE SSWG Challenge Team is developing a CubeSat Reference Model as a SysML logical framework for future CubeSat developers.
The reference model scope includes mission stakeholders, lifecycle stages from concept through retirement, and operations phases including launch, early operations, and normal operations.
The model incorporates needs, objectives, constraints, measures of effectiveness/performance, technical performance measures, requirements, and use cases with trace/refine/derive relationships.
The CubeSat enterprise is decomposed into space and ground systems plus external services such as ground-station services and transport/launch/deploy services.

The CubeSat logical architecture includes subsystems such as mission data acquisition/processing, communications, power, thermal, propulsion, command and data handling, guidance/navigation/control, attitude determination/control, and structures/mechanisms.
The Cal Poly CubeSat Design Specification was translated into a SysML model providing physical, mechanical, electrical, testing, and operational requirements.

Earlier phases modeled RAX mission behaviors including mission data collection/downlink, solar energy collection/storage, subsystem power consumption, and communications performance, and used executable behaviors/constraints for trade studies.
The distribution plan includes model files, video walk-throughs, copyright/licensing, MagicDraw, ZIP, XMI, OpenMBEE, Teamcenter, and user feedback mechanisms.
limitations_gaps: The paper states that the earlier FireSat example was hypothetical, so a real space system could not be built from that model and practical use could not be demonstrated or verified.
The CubeSat Reference Model is described as still maturing; future work includes refining model elements, verifying correctness, resolving copyright/licensing, and developing a release process.
No quantitative evaluation of reliability, reproducibility, or integrability outcomes is reported.
No EPS-specific verification procedure is described beyond the general power-subsystem architecture and prior energy modeling context.

quality.rationale: Credible conference venue with DOI and Space Symposium Technical Track identification. Limitations are only indirectly discussed through the FireSat verification limitation, current model maturity, and future verification/refinement plans; there is no formal threats-to-validity section.

evidence_quotes.claim: Paper purpose and MBSE reference-model status
evidence_quotes.quote: This paper reports on our current progress in the development of the CubeSat Reference Model and plans for the future.

evidence_quotes.claim: System model integrates discipline-specific models and simulations
evidence_quotes.quote: At the core of MBSE is the development of the system model that helps integrate other discipline-specific engineering models and simulations.

evidence_quotes.claim: Modeling language and broad CubeSat scope
evidence_quotes.quote: the team has been working to create a system model that captures many of the basic features of a CubeSat project using the Systems Modeling Language (SysML)

evidence_quotes.claim: Prior RAX simulation and trade-study context
evidence_quotes.quote: the team has created the initial iteration of the reference model, applied it to the Radio Aurora Explorer (RAX) mission, executed simulations of system behaviors, interfaced with commercial simulation tools, and demonstrated how behaviors and constraint equations can be executed to perform operational trade studies.

evidence_quotes.claim: MBSE supports requirements, analysis, verification, and validation
evidence_quotes.quote: MBSE is the formalized application of modeling to support key systems engineering tasks for addressing requirements, design, analysis, validation and verification.

requirements and interfaces are not contained in isolated engineering artifacts as done previously but are now integrated within a single system model. This allows for a full exploration of the model, and changes are automatically propagated and reflected in every view of the system.
The project's application of MBSE uses the Systems Modeling Language (SysML) and graphical modeling tools from No Magic.
SysML is modeling language which can support various system engineering methodologies including the methodology used by this team, Object-Oriented Systems Engineering Method (OOSEM)
The CubeSat Reference Model will provide the logical architecture. These logical elements can be reused for specifying a mission specific CubeSat.
A model for the power subsystem accounted for solar energy collection and storage and subsystem power consumption.
evidence_quotes.location: SSWG MBSE Challenge Project Early Phases

evidence_quotes.claim: Prior power and communications trade studies
evidence_quotes.quote: Two trade studies were demonstrated: 1) On-board energy level as a function of solar panel area and maximum battery capacity and 2) quantity of data downlinked as a function of orbital altitude and ground station network.
evidence_quotes.location: SSWG MBSE Challenge Project Early Phases

evidence_quotes.claim: Current reference-model scope includes lifecycle and operations
evidence_quotes.quote: The reference model can support all life cycle stages for a CubeSat mission. For example, for an academic CubeSat project, the likely stages would be concept, development, production, operational, and retirement. The model also supports all phases of operations: pre-launch integration and test, launch, early orbit checkout, and full mission operations.
evidence_quotes.location: Development of the CubeSat Reference Model

evidence_quotes.claim: Cal Poly requirements modeled, including electrical/testing/operations
evidence_quotes.quote: the translation of the Cal Poly CubeSat Design Specification documentation into a SysML model. This model provides the foundation for specifying a CubeSat's physical, mechanical, electrical, testing, and operational requirements.
evidence_quotes.location: Development of the CubeSat Reference Model

evidence_quotes.claim: Generic subsystem decomposition includes power subsystem
evidence_quotes.quote: The CubeSat Reference Model includes a general system decomposition that users can tailor to suit their particular project needs.
the SSWG team is developing a model distribution process to share to external entities
evidence_quotes.location: Distribution of the CubeSat Reference Model

evidence_quotes.quote: The future plans include: (i) refining the CubeSat Reference Model to include additional details for each of the model elements, (ii) verifying the correctness of the model, (iii) working with INCOSE on model copyright and licensing and (iv) developing a release plan and process for distributing the model.

evidence_quotes.claim: Claimed outcomes: reduced burden, checklist, uniformity/consistency
evidence_quotes.quote: MBSE holds the promise of reducing the burden of systems engineering tasks, which is beneficial to small CubeSat teams, and a properly designed reference model can serve as a checklist to these teams and promote uniformity and consistency across future CubeSat models.

evidence_quotes.claim: Explicit limitation of earlier hypothetical model
evidence_quotes.quote: the hypothetical nature of FireSat precluded anyone from actually building a real space system from the model. Therefore, the practical use of the model could not be demonstrated or verified.
evidence_quotes.location: SSWG MBSE Challenge Project Early Phases
